# Debt-track Disagreement Queue

**Module:** Debt Defense Prototype (all states/federal) - **Layer:** grounded-corroboration + adversarial-generation
**Runner rule:** `scripts/corroboration/run_corroboration.py` appends new flagged items only. It never edits or
overwrites the Resolution, Resolved by, or Date fields -- those belong to Andy / the certifying attorney.
Built per DEBT_PROJECT_ARCHITECTURE_SPEC.md S3(d), generalizing Direction D-2 (`docs/DIRECTION_D_ROADMAP.md`) into
the debt track, per the 2026-08-26 Phase-A-Unblock direction item 6.

> **How to use this queue:** work top-to-bottom. Each entry has a candidate classification (rule gap / model error /
> citation-aggregator error) computed mechanically by the runner as a *hint*, not a determination -- the runner does
> not and cannot decide which side is legally correct. Fill in Resolution and Resolved-by, then move to Resolved.

  - claude-opus-5: grounded=True, error=None, summary="Under Cal. Code Civ. Proc. § 412.20(a)(3), the summons must direct the defendant to file a written pleading responding to the complaint within 30 days after the summons is served, and § 412.20(a)(6) repeats that warning ('you respond within 30 days'). If no response is filed, § 412.20(a)(4) says default may be entered on the plaintiff's application and the plaintiff may obtain the relief demanded, including wage garnishment or taking of money or property. When the 30 days begins depends on how service is completed: substituted service and out-of-state mail service are deemed complete on the 10th day after mailing (§§ 415.20, 415.40), and service by publication is deemed complete on the 28th day after the first publication (§ 415.50). A defendant contesting jurisdiction may, on or before that last day to plead (or a longer period the court allows for good cause), file a motion to quash service without that filing counting as an appearance unless the motion is denied (§ 418.10)."

Proc. § 412.20(a)(3)-(4) and (a)(6), the summons must direct the defendant to file a written pleading responding to the complaint within 30 days after the summons is served, and must warn that otherwise a default may be entered and the court may decide against the defendant without hearing them, potentially leading to wage garnishment or seizure of money or property. Instead of (or in addition to) a pleading, a defendant may, on or before the last day to plead — or within further time the court allows for good cause — file a motion to quash service for lack of jurisdiction under § 418.10, which does not count as an appearance unless the motion is denied."

For substituted service and service outside California by mail, service is deemed complete on the 10th day after mailing; for publication, service is deemed complete on the 28th day after the first day of publication.'
